clue.text: Boy in academy starts to court daughter, 14

parts.note: Victor is a boy's name

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letters of the words in and academy

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A schoolboy at an academy begins wooing a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the first letters of 'in academy', giving IA. The definition is a cross-reference: 14 down is COMEDIENNE, and Victoria Wood was a much-loved British comic writer and performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Wood was a celebrated British comic performer and writer, so she is an example of a female comic.

clue.text: Knock fashionable name in German society

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Criticising a trendy name in German high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' is a cricket term: a batsman's innings, a spell at the crease, is also called a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a knock is a batsman's innings, the period spent batting.

clue.text: Women omitted from message before democrat wavered

indicators.note: omitted from says the women's letter is dropped from the message

parts.note: a tweet is a message posted online
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A post with women cut out was sent before a Democrat changed their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitted from' removes W from TWEET, leaving TEET.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to sway unsteadily, as something that wavered moved back and forth.

clue.text: Arena psychiatrist leaves quietly!

indicators.note: leaves says the quiet sound departs from the slang word

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist slips out of the stadium unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes SH from SHRINK.
explanation.definitionFit: A rink is an enclosed area for skating or curling, a kind of arena.

clue.text: Draw drivers in amateur races into error

indicators.note: in puts the motorists' club inside the rest

parts.note: the TT races are the Isle of Man motorcycle races

indicators.note: error says the letters of into are set down wrongly

parts.note: the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motorists' organisation

explanation.surface: Motorists in amateur racing are drawn into a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges INTO to TION; 'in' puts RAC inside A, TT and TION. The RAC is a British motoring club; the TT is the Isle of Man race.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is something that attracts crowds, an attraction.

clue.text: Apparently there's no charge to make speech

parts.note: O stands for nought, no
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: It seems you can give a speech for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' hints that the answer split as O RATE looks like a zero rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech.

clue.text: Woodwind lessons somewhat in decline

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Woodwind tuition is falling off somewhat.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to shrink gradually, to decline.

clue.text: Musical article featuring my old pieces

indicators.note: featuring has the article take the exclamation inside it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
cor! is a British exclamation like my!
antiques are old pieces of furniture or ornament

explanation.surface: A musical item featuring some old pieces of mine.
explanation.walkthrough: Acorn Antiques was Victoria Wood's spoof soap, later a stage musical; 'cor' is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Acorn Antiques: The Musical was Victoria Wood's West End stage show, built on her spoof soap opera.

clue.text: Band fared badly with randy couple in song

parts.note: a bar is a band or stripe of colour

indicators.note: badly says the letters of fared and randy together are jumbled

explanation.surface: A group did poorly with a lustful pair who feature in a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like the musicians; it is BAR, a stripe. 'badly' rearranges FARED with RANDY. The song is Victoria Wood's comic number Let's Do It, about a couple of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Wood's comic song tells of a pair, one eager and one reluctant, so the names identify that duo.

clue.text: College worker spotted without son in cafeteria

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's classic worker insect

indicators.note: without tells us to remove the son's letter from the word for spotted

parts.note: spotted means seen
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A college employee was seen in the cafeteria without their son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes S (son) from SEEN, leaving EEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria-style dining room in a workplace, school or barracks.

clue.text: Sort of small tiara worn by northern empress

indicators.note: sort of here means sort out, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A small tiara of a kind worn by a northern empress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' signals an anagram of S, TIARA and N together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar, or a female ruler of Russia, so effectively an empress.

clue.text: Managed, for example, to return kitchen appliance

parts.note: ran a business means managed it

indicators.note: to return says the abbreviation for for example is written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone managed, for instance, to send a cooker back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large cooking stove, a standard piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Theatrical end arguably has hidden agenda

indicators.note: has hidden says the answer sits concealed inside the run of words before it

explanation.surface: A dramatic ending might well conceal an ulterior motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden agenda' reads as a stock phrase, but 'has hidden' is the signal and 'agenda' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a schedule of events or business, as an agenda is a list of things to be dealt with.

clue.text: Approach finish in anger, regularly showing female wit

parts.note: to come is to approach
to die is to come to an end

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of in anger

explanation.surface: Someone nears the end of an outburst, repeatedly showing a woman's sharp humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedienne is a woman who makes people laugh, a female wit.

clue.text: Working in jumping event following horse show

indicators.note: following puts the jumping event after the horse

parts.note: an ass is a member of the horse family

indicators.note: in places the word for working inside the rearranged event
jumping says the letters of event leap about into a new order

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A rider is competing in a show-jumping event after a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' rearranges EVENT to EENTV, and 'in' puts ON inside it, after ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used of products advertised on television, and here it stands for a show on screen.

clue.text: Maybe second opinion given before answer

parts.note: my bet is means in my opinion

explanation.surface: A second opinion is sought before an answer is given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' shows second is only one example: beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, and a second-ranked grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet and denotes second place in a ranking.

clue.text: Touching on idea originally blocked by part of suit?

indicators.note: blocked by means the rearranged letters are interrupted by the clothing
originally says the letters of on idea are put together in a new and original way

parts.note: a DJ, dinner jacket, is part of a dinner suit

explanation.surface: Raising an idea first on a lawsuit, which is held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' rearranges ON IDEA to AOINED, and 'blocked by' puts DJ inside it after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that adjoined were next to and in contact with each other.

clue.text: Right turn used now and again

indicators.note: now and again picks out every other letter of turn used

explanation.surface: A right turn taken only occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: True and right are synonyms for correct or accurate.

clue.text: As one, peacekeepers provided international education

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers united to provide international education.
explanation.definitionFit: Unified means combined into a whole, acting together as one.

clue.text: Indirectly, Mo Farah's last — so what?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: last calls for the final letter of the runner's surname

parts.note: And? is a dismissive way of saying so what?

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off Mo Farah finishing last in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Farah is the British distance runner; 'Mo' is really a short moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something second-hand means getting it through someone else rather than directly.

clue.text: Way a European embraces preacher

indicators.note: embraces has the European take the way inside

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: On the road a European hugs a preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts ST inside POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a missionary or disciple who spreads a faith, a preacher.

clue.text: Impractical to abandon mostly toxic rubbish

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter of the word for abandon

parts.note: to quit a place is to abandon it

indicators.note: rubbish says the letters of toxic are a mess to be reordered

explanation.surface: It is unrealistic to abandon most toxic waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts QUIT to QUI; 'rubbish' rearranges TOXIC to XOTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Quixotic, after Don Quixote, means idealistic to the point of being unrealistic.

clue.text: One getting battered in ring?

parts.note: reads as a boxer taking a beating, but means a vegetable slice fried in batter as a ring

explanation.surface: A boxer taking a pounding in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Battered means coated in batter: rings of this vegetable are fried that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Onion rings are slices of the bulb coated in batter and deep-fried.

clue.text: Savour old party game making a comeback

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: making a comeback says the game's letters run the other way

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Relishing an old party game that is back in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns RU into UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Savour as a noun is a smell or taste, as an odour is a scent.

clue.text: Principal characters in Let's Do It welcoming love over god

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the whole is read upwards
welcoming has those letters take the zero score inside
principal characters means the first letters of the words of the song title

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: The song Let's Do It, featuring the main characters, puts love above God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let's Do It' gives LDI; 'welcoming' adds O to make LODI, and 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Lie about issue over current omission

indicators.note: about says the letters of lie are turned around into another order
over has the word for issue covering the current, so it goes round it

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A lie about a matter that skates over a current omission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIE into ELI; 'over' has SON go round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Elision is the leaving out of a sound or syllable in speech, a kind of omission.

clue.text: Marked negative temperature in document

indicators.note: in puts the negative and temperature inside the document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
no is a negative

explanation.surface: A negative temperature was marked in a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Denoted means indicated or signified, as something marked is shown by a sign.

clue.text: Sitcom director's secret ideals misplaced

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for director
inner thoughts are private, secret ones

indicators.note: misplaced says the letters of ideals are put in the wrong places

explanation.surface: A film director's private ideals have gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' rearranges IDEALS into LADIES. Dinnerladies was Victoria Wood's BBC sitcom set in a works canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinnerladies is the title of Victoria Wood's television comedy series about canteen staff.
